return this.http.get(this.hostServer + '/rest/user/change-password?current=' + passwords.current + '&new=' +
    passwords.new + '&repeat=' + passwords.repeat).pipe(map((response: any) => response.user), catchError((err) => { throw err.error }))

context.guidance: Keep Personal Data out of application, access and error logs. Write an opaque identifier or a masked form in place of each value, and strip request bodies and query strings before a log line is written. Where a value must be recorded, apply a protection that Rule 6(1)(a) names, such as encryption, obfuscation, masking or a virtual token. Apply the same rule to logging middleware and to any external log sink.

value.fix: Stop sending the passwords in the URL. They currently travel in the query string of a GET request (`/rest/user/change-password?current=...&new=...&repeat=...`), so they get written in plain text to server access logs, proxy and load-balancer logs, browser history and any external log sink. Change the client call to a POST (or PUT) and put the values in the request body: `return this.http.post(this.hostServer + '/rest/user/change-password', { current: passwords.current, new: passwords.new, repeat: passwords.repeat }).pipe(map((response: any) => response.user), catchError((err) => { throw err.error }))`. On the server, register the matching POST route, read the values from `req.body`, and drop the old GET route so nothing can keep sending passwords in the URL. The endpoint must only be reachable over HTTPS. Make sure the logging middleware (for example morgan or express access logs) and any error handler never write request bodies, and that they hide or remove fields like `current`, `new`, `repeat` and `password` before a log line is written. Also hide or remove query strings from logged URLs, so any old clients that still use the GET form don't leak the values. In the `catchError` path, don't log or send the request payload back. Where a log entry is needed for auditing, record only an opaque user ID or token and the outcome, never the password values.
